newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - APIs bolster crude, drag refined products. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - APIs bolster crude, drag refined products. [CORRECTED 15:25 GMT]

text.p: U.S. traders interpreted new American Petroleum Institute data bearishly for refined oil products but said an athletic 2.3 percent jump in refinery utilization could prove supportive for crude oil.
Indeed, April gasoline futures fell about 0.37 cent in after-hours ACCESS trade while heat dipped 0.28 cent at 1852 EST (2352 GMT) on data for the week ending March 21.

"The sharp jump in refinery utilization was a bit unexpected" said Tom Bentz of ING Derivatives Clearing Inc, noting the API report released late Tuesday showed utilization vaulting to 92.7 percent from 90.4 percent the prior week.
Many traders had predicted the utilization rate would edge up only a half-percentage point as Gulf Coast refineries continued to come back from maintenance turnarounds.

Bentz predicted the higher utilization rate would be "slightly supportive" for crude, with total U.S. stocks falling 2.2 million barrels for the week although year-on-year inventories were up 3.3 million barrels.

April crude edged a bit higher in ACCESS trade, with the market perhaps seeing the utilizaton data as evidence refiners are ramping up to build gasoline stocks for the approaching driving season which traditionally begins Memorial Day in late May.
The data showed total gasoline stocks building 1.1 million barrels, contrary to predictions stocks would shrink.
"With runs coming up, it looks a little bearish for gasoline," one Gulf trader said.

Another trader said he considered the gasoline build "seasonally normal," and predicted prices would be supported by API data estimating total U.S. stocks 7.8 million barrels shy of last year's already low levels.
East Coast reformulated gasoline grades fell by 1.9 million barrels for the week, putting them almost 5.5 million barrels below the same week last year.
"It might be a little bullish on RFGs and support the Merc," one player said, adding New York Mercantile Exchange futures were based on East Coast reformulated specifications.
The API data showed distillate stocks declining by 1.3 million barrels, including a 1.0 million barrel draw on heating oil and a 332,000 barrel fall in low sulfur diesel.
"I call that bearish," one broker said, saying the distillate draw paled in comparison with a 5-million-barrel draw for the same week last year.
Furthermore, total distillate stocks now stand 11.1 million barrels above last year's levels.
